title: Lena plans an exhibition
topic: A museum guide named Lena prepares an exhibition of old portraits; the show opens on Saturday
tail_E: Admission costs five euros, so every visitor buys a
target_note: 'ticket' is the natural continuation of 'every visitor buys a' in a museum/exhibition context where admission is charged; the word occurs nowhere in the units or the tail, and neither does its German equivalent (Eintrittskarte / Ticket / Karte). ' ticket' is a single Pythia token (id 13571); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.23, next candidate 'copy' ~ 0.08).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (F01A, museum guide Lena)
notes: Formulation A. Ten meaning units: Lena plans an exhibition / the director picks the theme / assistants carry frames / Lena measures the walls / the oldest portrait shows a Hamburg merchant / a restorer repairs a crack / the lamps light the paintings / Lena writes labels / a journalist writes about the show / the exhibition begins. German predicates avoid separable verbs (no particle stranded before the adjunct); 'vorbereiten' was therefore replaced by 'planen' in unit 1. Subjects alternate between the protagonist, other people (director, assistants, restorer, journalist) and objects (portrait, lamps, exhibition), with singular and plural, so C3 switches cross real agreement boundaries. 'Hamburg' and 'Lena' are the only proper names and are identical in both languages. Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
